1.title: Prologue and Vision of the Glorified Christ
1.themes: Revelation, prophecy, the eternal nature of God, Christ's glory and majesty.
1.outline:
I. Prologue (1:1-3)
II. Greetings and Doxology (1:4-8)
III. John's Vision of Christ (1:9-20)
1.summary: John receives a revelation from Jesus Christ, intended to show God's servants what must soon take place. Exiled on Patmos, John hears a loud voice and turns to see a vision of the glorified Christ standing among seven golden lampstands, holding seven stars. Christ instructs John to write down what he sees and send it to the seven churches.

2.title: Messages to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, and Thyatira
2.themes: Repentance, endurance in suffering, resisting false teaching, holding fast to faith.
2.outline:
I. Message to Ephesus (2:1-7)
II. Message to Smyrna (2:8-11)
III. Message to Pergamum (2:12-17)
IV. Message to Thyatira (2:18-29)
2.summary: Christ dictates specific messages for four of the seven churches in Asia. He praises Ephesus for their hard work but rebukes them for losing their first love. He encourages Smyrna in their impending persecution. He rebukes Pergamum for tolerating false teachings (Balaam and the Nicolaitans). He rebukes Thyatira for tolerating the false prophetess Jezebel.

3.title: Messages to Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea
3.themes: Spiritual deadness, divine protection, lukewarm faith, urgent call to repentance.
3.outline:
I. Message to Sardis (3:1-6)
II. Message to Philadelphia (3:7-13)
III. Message to Laodicea (3:14-22)
3.summary: Christ continues His messages to the final three churches. Sardis is rebuked for being spiritually dead despite having a reputation for being alive. Philadelphia is commended for keeping God's word and is promised an open door and protection. Laodicea is strongly rebuked for being spiritually lukewarm, self-sufficient, and blind to their true spiritual poverty.

4.title: The Throne in Heaven
4.themes: God's sovereignty, heavenly worship, God's holiness as Creator.
4.outline:
I. The Open Door and the Throne (4:1-6a)
II. The Four Living Creatures and Twenty-Four Elders (4:6b-11)
4.summary: John is taken up in the Spirit to heaven and sees a door open. He witnesses the glorious throne of God, surrounded by a rainbow, twenty-four elders, and four living creatures. Day and night, they continually worship the Lord God Almighty, praising Him for His holiness and His work of creation.

5.title: The Scroll and the Lamb
5.themes: Christ's worthiness, redemption through His blood, universal worship.
5.outline:
I. The Sealed Scroll (5:1-4)
II. The Worthy Lamb (5:5-10)
III. All Creation Worships (5:11-14)
5.summary: John sees a scroll sealed with seven seals in God's right hand. He weeps because no one is found worthy to open it. An elder tells him that the Lion of the tribe of Judah has triumphed. John then sees a Lamb, looking as if it had been slain. The Lamb takes the scroll, prompting universal worship from the living creatures, elders, angels, and all creation.

6.title: The Seals
6.themes: Divine judgment, conquest, war, famine, death, the cry of the martyrs, the wrath of the Lamb.
6.outline:
I. The First Four Seals: The Four Horsemen (6:1-8)
II. The Fifth Seal: The Martyrs (6:9-11)
III. The Sixth Seal: Cosmic Disturbances (6:12-17)
6.summary: The Lamb begins to open the seals. The first four bring forth the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, representing conquest, war, famine, and death. The fifth seal reveals the souls of martyrs under the altar crying out for justice. The sixth seal causes massive cosmic disturbances and natural disasters, causing all classes of humanity to hide from the wrath of God and the Lamb.

7.title: The 144,000 and the Great Multitude
7.themes: Divine protection, salvation, ultimate comfort, tribulation.
7.outline:
I. Sealing of the 144,000 (7:1-8)
II. The Great Multitude in White Robes (7:9-17)
7.summary: Before further judgments, angels hold back the four winds of the earth until the servants of God are sealed on their foreheads; John hears their number is 144,000 from the tribes of Israel. Then he sees an uncountable multitude from every nation standing before the throne, clothed in white. They are those who have come out of the great tribulation, and God wipes every tear from their eyes.

8.title: The Seventh Seal and the Trumpets
8.themes: Silence in heaven, prayers of the saints, catastrophic judgments on the earth.
8.outline:
I. The Seventh Seal and the Golden Censer (8:1-5)
II. The First Four Trumpets (8:6-13)
8.summary: When the Lamb opens the seventh seal, there is silence in heaven for about half an hour. An angel offers the prayers of the saints with incense, then hurls the censer to earth, causing thunder and an earthquake. Seven angels prepare to sound their trumpets. The first four trumpets bring devastation to the earth's vegetation, the seas, the fresh waters, and the heavenly bodies.

9.title: The Fifth and Sixth Trumpets
9.themes: Demonic torment, divine limits on evil, judgment, human impenitence.
9.outline:
I. The Fifth Trumpet: The Plague of Locusts (9:1-12)
II. The Sixth Trumpet: The Angels from the Euphrates (9:13-21)
9.summary: The fifth trumpet sounds, releasing a swarm of demonic locusts from the Abyss led by Apollyon to torment those without God's seal for five months. The sixth trumpet releases four angels bound at the Euphrates River, along with a massive demonic cavalry that kills a third of mankind. Despite these severe judgments, the survivors refuse to repent of their idolatry and wickedness.

10.title: The Angel and the Little Scroll
10.themes: Prophetic commission, the mystery of God, sweet and bitter message.
10.outline:
I. The Mighty Angel (10:1-7)
II. John Eats the Scroll (10:8-11)
10.summary: A mighty angel descends from heaven holding a little scroll. He stands on the sea and land, swearing that there will be no more delay and that the mystery of God will be accomplished when the seventh trumpet sounds. John is instructed to take and eat the little scroll; it tastes sweet as honey in his mouth but turns sour in his stomach, symbolizing his renewed prophetic commission.

11.title: The Two Witnesses and the Seventh Trumpet
11.themes: Prophetic witness, martyrdom, vindication, God's eternal reign.
11.outline:
I. Measuring the Temple (11:1-2)
II. The Two Witnesses (11:3-14)
III. The Seventh Trumpet (11:15-19)
11.summary: John is given a reed to measure the temple. Two witnesses are granted power to prophesy for 1,260 days, shutting the sky and bringing plagues. They are ultimately killed by the beast from the Abyss, their bodies left in the street. After three and a half days, God resurrects them and takes them to heaven. The seventh trumpet then sounds, declaring that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of the Lord and of His Christ.

12.title: The Woman and the Dragon
12.themes: Cosmic conflict, Satan's hostility toward God's people, divine protection.
12.outline:
I. The Woman, the Child, and the Dragon (12:1-6)
II. War in Heaven (12:7-12)
III. The Dragon Persecutes the Woman (12:13-17)
12.summary: A great sign appears in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun about to give birth, and a red dragon waiting to devour her child. She gives birth to a male child (Christ), who is snatched up to God. War breaks out in heaven; Michael and his angels defeat the dragon (Satan), throwing him down to earth. Enraged, the dragon pursues the woman and makes war against her offspring.

13.title: The Two Beasts
13.themes: Antichrist, false religion, persecution, the mark of the beast, endurance.
13.outline:
I. The Beast out of the Sea (13:1-10)
II. The Beast out of the Earth (13:11-18)
13.summary: John sees a beast rising out of the sea with seven heads and ten horns, empowered by the dragon to blaspheme God and conquer the saints. The whole world marvels and worships it. A second beast rises from the earth, performing deceptive miracles and forcing all people to worship the first beast. It decrees that everyone must receive a mark (666) on their right hand or forehead to buy or sell.

14.title: The Lamb and the 144,000, and the Harvest
14.themes: Purity, divine judgment, the eternal gospel, reaping the earth.
14.outline:
I. The Lamb and the 144,000 (14:1-5)
II. The Three Angels' Messages (14:6-13)
III. Reaping the Earth's Harvest (14:14-20)
14.summary: John sees the Lamb standing on Mount Zion with the 144,000 who are pure and redeemed, singing a new song. Three angels proclaim messages: the eternal gospel, the fall of Babylon, and a warning against taking the mark of the beast. Finally, a vision of two harvests is shown—the Son of Man reaping the grain harvest of the earth, and an angel reaping the grape harvest of God's wrath.

15.title: Seven Angels with Seven Plagues
15.themes: God's righteous judgments, preparation for wrath, worship.
15.outline:
I. The Song of Moses and the Lamb (15:1-4)
II. Preparation of the Bowls of Wrath (15:5-8)
15.summary: John sees seven angels holding the seven last plagues. Those who have been victorious over the beast stand beside a sea of glass, singing the song of Moses and the Lamb, praising God's justice. The temple in heaven is opened, and the seven angels receive seven golden bowls filled with the wrath of God. The temple fills with smoke, and no one can enter until the plagues are completed.

16.title: The Seven Bowls of God's Wrath
16.themes: Final and complete judgment, human stubbornness, Armageddon.
16.outline:
I. The First Three Bowls (16:1-7)
II. The Next Three Bowls (16:8-16)
III. The Seventh Bowl (16:17-21)
16.summary: A loud voice commands the seven angels to pour out the bowls of God's wrath. The plagues bring sores, turn the seas and rivers to blood, scorch people with fire, and plunge the beast's kingdom into darkness. Despite the agony, people refuse to repent. Demonic spirits gather the kings of the world for the battle of Armageddon. The final bowl causes an unprecedented global earthquake and massive hailstones.

17.title: The Great Prostitute and the Beast
17.themes: Spiritual adultery, oppressive world systems, the allure and doom of Babylon.
17.outline:
I. Vision of the Great Prostitute (17:1-6)
II. The Mystery Explained (17:7-18)
17.summary: An angel shows John the judgment of the great prostitute, Babylon, who sits on many waters and rides a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns. She is drunk with the blood of the saints. The angel explains that the beast's heads represent kings/mountains and the horns represent future kings who will ally with the beast, eventually turning against the prostitute to destroy her, fulfilling God's purpose.

18.title: The Fall of Babylon
18.themes: Economic collapse, divine justice, separation from worldly corruption.
18.outline:
I. The Announcement of Babylon's Fall (18:1-3)
II. Call to Separate from Her (18:4-8)
III. Lament over Babylon (18:9-19)
IV. Heaven Rejoices (18:20-24)
18.summary: A mighty angel declares that Babylon the Great has fallen. A voice from heaven urges God's people to flee from her to avoid sharing in her sins and plagues. The kings, merchants, and sailors of the earth mourn her sudden destruction because their source of wealth is gone. In contrast, heaven and the saints are called to rejoice over her righteous judgment.

19.title: Rejoicing in Heaven and the Rider on the White Horse
19.themes: Praise, the marriage of the Lamb, righteous warfare, victory of Christ.
19.outline:
I. Hallelujah Chorus (19:1-5)
II. The Marriage Supper of the Lamb (19:6-10)
III. The Rider on the White Horse Defeats the Beast (19:11-21)
19.summary: A great multitude in heaven shouts 'Hallelujah!' praising God for judging the prostitute and bringing about the marriage of the Lamb to His prepared bride. John then sees heaven open and Christ appearing as a rider on a white horse, named Faithful and True, the Word of God. He leads the armies of heaven to strike down the nations, capturing the beast and the false prophet, throwing them into the lake of fire.

20.title: The Millennium and the Final Judgment
20.themes: The binding of Satan, Christ's reign, final defeat of evil, the Great White Throne.
20.outline:
I. Satan Bound and the Millennial Reign (20:1-6)
II. Satan's Final Defeat (20:7-10)
III. The Great White Throne Judgment (20:11-15)
20.summary: An angel binds Satan in the Abyss for a thousand years, during which resurrected saints reign with Christ. Afterward, Satan is released and deceives the nations (Gog and Magog) for one final battle, but fire from heaven consumes them, and Satan is thrown into the lake of fire permanently. Then, all the dead stand before the Great White Throne for final judgment; anyone whose name is not in the book of life is cast into the lake of fire.

21.title: The New Heaven and the New Earth
21.themes: Restoration, eternal dwelling of God with humanity, glory of the New Jerusalem.
21.outline:
I. All Things Made New (21:1-8)
II. The New Jerusalem Described (21:9-21)
III. The Glory of the City (21:22-27)
21.summary: John sees a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and earth have passed away. The Holy City, the New Jerusalem, descends from heaven. God dwells intimately with His people, wiping away every tear and eliminating death and pain. An angel shows John the city's magnificent structure—its glowing jasper walls, pearly gates, and foundations of precious stones. It needs no sun or moon, for God's glory illuminates it.

22.title: Eden Restored and Jesus Is Coming
22.themes: Eternal life, the river of life, the imminent return of Christ, invitation and warning.
22.outline:
I. The River and Tree of Life (22:1-5)
II. Final Reminders and Exhortations (22:6-17)
III. Final Warning and Benediction (22:18-21)
22.summary: The angel shows John the river of the water of life flowing from God's throne, with the tree of life bearing fruit on its banks, reversing the curse of Eden. God's servants will see His face and reign forever. The book closes with strong affirmations that Jesus is coming soon. A final invitation is given to all who are thirsty to take the free gift of the water of life, accompanied by a warning not to add or take away from the prophecy.
